payload.title: A deploy refuses to silently remove a deployed optional feature
payload.description:
Found while landing #1429 (optional backend features default off). A deploy whose synthesized flags turn a feature off removes that feature's resources: the console responder function and Message stream trigger, the inbound email receipt rule, functions and EventBridge rules, the storage backup plan. No table or bucket goes, but mail to a removed inbound address bounces and backups silently stop.

Guard in `papyrus-infra backend-deploy`: before deploying, read the deployed root stack outputs (the `inboundEmail`, `storageBackups` and console responder entries, the way cost-tag waves already read PapyrusCostTagWave), compare them with the synthesized flags, and refuse the deploy, naming the feature, unless the site writes that feature as an explicit `false` in papyrus.config.ts. A feature that was never deployed is unaffected. No fallback and no override flag.

Gherkin:
Feature: A deploy never silently removes a deployed feature
  Scenario: Inbound email is deployed and the synthesized flag is off by default
    Given the deployed root stack reports inbound email on
    And the site does not write features.inboundEmail
    When backend-deploy runs
    Then it refuses before changing anything, naming inboundEmail and how to keep or remove it
  Scenario: The site writes the feature as an explicit false
    Given the deployed root stack reports storage backups on
    And the site writes features.storageBackups as false
    When backend-deploy runs
    Then the deploy proceeds
  Scenario: A feature that was never deployed
    Given the deployed root stack reports the console responder off
    When backend-deploy runs with it off
    Then the deploy proceeds
  Scenario: A first deploy
    Given no root stack exists
    Then there is nothing to compare and the deploy proceeds

Needs a gated AWS test (the stack outputs come from a real deployed stack); unit-test the comparison with recorded outputs.
